extraction.Name: George Bartlett
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not desire his patent in fee at the time he accepted it, for the reason that he did not want to pay taxes; that he received a letter from the Indian Agency, stating that his patent in fee was in this Office; that he answered back that he did not want the patent in fee; and that he later received a registered letter from the Indian Agency, enclosing patent in fee to his allotment, and advising that it was necessary that he accept it, which he did, signing for same
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Mortgaged and sold; about 1920, he traded this allotment of 160 acres to Albert Morton for another 160; in 1927, he sold the place to Roy Searby, of Wanblee, South Dakota, for Sixteen Hundred Dollars ($1600.00), Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) of this amount being absorbed by a mortgage given to Frank Alberts, of Presho, South Dakota, for improvements on place and farm implements necessary for carrying on farming
extraction.Buyer: Sold to Roy Searby, of Wanblee, South Dakota, for $1600.00; mortgage given to Frank Alberts, of Presho, South Dakota
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: had to sell it through the force of circumstances; does not consider that $1600.00 was a fair price for the land
extraction.Occupation/Income: income is about $500.00 per year, earned by being a printer for the United States Government, and this is his only revenue
extraction.NOTES: File No. 5563; mentally competent; enjoying fair health — is bothered with rheumatism; has a wife and six minor children to support; health of entire family is good except one child, who had pneumonia and has never been well since; has never received any aid from the Government or County; affidavit subscribed and sworn to November 12, 1928; document appears to be continuation of a prior deponent's statement before Bartlett's testimony begins | TASK 5 CAT_3 BACKFILL 2026-05-04 (patents database): Allotment 5563 sourced from federal-register-app patents database (Christian's research, 2026-05-04).
